transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Ruth Patel (Lyon - Head of Search), Ethan Cole (Lyon - ML Eng), Nora Singh (Lyon - Infra)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Lyon's current retrieval pipeline, constraints around throughput and latency, and whether Redwood Hosted or Dedicated (or Private) is appropriate for an embeddings + rerank architecture. Customer wants hybrid search (BM25 + vector) with a two-stage reranker and low 100s-ms P95 SLA for user-facing queries.

Topics covered:
- Current stack (OpenSearch + in-house vector)
- Vector dimensionality and embedding model choices
- Throughput requirements and peak QPS
- Vector DB integration approaches (hosted vs external Pinecone/Weaviate vs OpenSearch)
- Reranking architecture and latency tradeoffs
- Security / VPC / KMS requirements
- Next steps: benchmark and pricing for Dedicated pilot

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Maya on the sales side, and Diego on the call is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Ruth (Lyon): Hi, Ruth here. I run search at Lyon. We've got Ethan and Nora on the line as well.
[00:17] Ethan (Lyon): Hi all.
[00:19] Nora (Lyon): Hello.
[00:22] Diego (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. Ruth, real quick can you give us the high-level of what you're trying to solve with embeddings and rerank?
[00:30] Ruth: Sure. So we currently do a hybrid search: BM25 from OpenSearch for recall and then we do an in-house embed + cosine rerank. It works but it's getting expensive and slow at scale. We want to evaluate moving embeddings and rerank into a managed flow so product search latency stays under 300ms P95 and cost is lower.
[00:48] Maya: Helpful. What's your current qps and peak traffic patterns?
[00:52] Ruth: Normal is 60 QPS, peaks to ~700 during promotions. Typical query size is short, user typed queries, but we also support semantic query expansion.
[01:05] Ethan: Our rerank model is a small transformer, runs on CPU right now but it's CPU-bound and we see 200-400ms additional latency per request when reranking 50 candidates.
[01:18] Diego: Got it. Two typical architecture levers: 1) move embedding generation and nearest neighbor search to a vector DB with fast ANN, or 2) keep vector store in OpenSearch but use Redwood to serve embeddings and do the rerank on dedicated GPUs to reduce latency. Any preference?
[01:35] Ruth: We prefer to avoid major re-architecture; ideally we keep OpenSearch for BM25 and plug in an external ANN for the vector step. But if Redwood's Dedicated offering can host embeddings and reranker with VPC and talk to our OpenSearch, that's interesting.
[01:52] Nora: Security is key - we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS support. Any on-prem or private cloud options?
[02:00] Maya: Absolutely, we support Hosted (fastest to start), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with VPC peering), and Private for on-prem/air-gapped. SOC2 and KMS integrations are available for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has SOC2 controls and configurable data retention.
[02:15] Ethan: For embeddings dimensionality - we're currently using 768 dims from our in-house model. Some experiments used 1536 dims and qdrant handled it fine but the vector size change increased storage and index build time. What does Redwood recommend?
[02:31] Diego: There's a tradeoff. Higher dims can help quality but increase cost and index cost. If you plan to do rerank with a transformer second stage, you can often get away with 768 or even 384 in a two-stage setup. We'll run benchmarks with your sample to validate.
[02:46] Ruth: About vector DBs - our infra team has experience with OpenSearch kNN and a small Pinecone pilot. We like Pinecone's managed ops but worried about vendor lock and cost. Does Redwood integrate directly with Pinecone/Weaviate/OpenSearch?
[03:02] Maya: Yes, you can use Redwood Hosted/Dedicated for generating embeddings and reranking, and either 1) store vectors in your preferred vector DB and call it from your app, or 2) use Redwood's managed nearest-neighbor service in Hosted mode. For Dedicated, most customers run their vector DB in their VPC (Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, OpenSearch) and we peer.
[03:20] Nora: Latency wise, do we incur network RTT to your service for a P95 under 300ms?
[03:26] Diego: With Dedicated in your VPC, we can get sub-50ms for embedding generation and sub-100ms for ANN lookup depending on your cluster config; rerank on GPU can be 20-60ms depending on model size. Hosted adds network overhead - still often under 200-300ms for US regions, but depends on peering.
[03:44] Ethan: For our peak of 700 qps, what batching/throughput options exist? We don't want to exceed budget.
[03:51] Diego: We recommend Dedicated with autoscaling and configured batching. Continuous batching in the runtime can increase throughput by 3-10x for embeddings; for rerank it's more sensitive because of latency SLOs so you size GPU pools for tail. We'll provide guidance and a cost model.
[04:08] Ruth: How do you handle rerank candidates? We do top-k retrieval from BM25 and ANN then rerank. Any constraints on k?
[04:14] Diego: Typical pattern is k=100 for recall, then rerank top 10 or 20. Redwood supports that two-stage flow; you can do a hybrid retrieve (BM25 + ANN merge) and then send the top candidates to a GPU-backed reranker API.
[04:28] Maya: Quick question on embeddings model: do you want us to host a specific model, or do you plan to use your own model for embeddings?
[04:35] Ethan: We have an in-house embedder but are open to standard models if they give better vectors. We'll likely test both.
[04:41] Diego: Great - we can host customer models in Dedicated (with pinned versions) or use Redwood-curated models. We also support quantized variants to lower memory for large dims.
[04:50] Nora: Regarding compliance, can we keep logs and telemetry inside our account and control retention? Auditors ask for proof of deletion sometimes.
[04:58] Maya: Yes, Dedicated and Private give customer-controlled logs and retention. We also integrate with KMS/HSM for key management. Hosted offers configurable retention and export of audit logs.
[05:08] Ruth: At a high level, we're leaning to Dedicated if the cost looks reasonable. Key blockers are pricing, VPC peering complexity, and onboarding effort.
[05:18] Diego: Understood. For pricing, we usually propose a 3-month pilot with reserved GPU capacity sized for your peak QPS with a runoff for autoscaling. We'll size based on your sample and run a benchmark.
[05:30] Ethan: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[05:33] Diego: A representative sample of documents and the vectors (if you can export), plus query log for a 24h period to model load. If you can't export vectors, we'll generate embeddings from sample text using the model you want to test.
[05:46] Ruth: We can provide 1M document sample and a 24h query trace. Nora will share the S3 bucket link.
[05:53] Nora: I'll upload the sample and share credentials for a read-only S3 access.
[05:58] Maya: Great. We'll run two benchmarks: 1) Hosted flow with Redwood generating embeddings and using your Pinecone/managed DB, 2) Dedicated with VPC peering and reranker on GPU. We'll measure P50/P95 latencies and cost per 1000 queries.
[06:12] Ruth: About hybrid search - any suggestions for merging BM25 scores with ANN similarity? We want rules, not black box.
[06:18] Diego: Common approach is score normalization and linear blending with tunable alpha. Another is use BM25 to ensure recall and then use ANN for reranking. We can help set up a small eval harness and metrics (MRR, NDCG) tied to your ground truth.
[06:32] Ethan: How about dimensionality - if we drop to 384 it's cheaper but what's the expected quality hit?
[06:37] Diego: It depends on model and data. For product queries, 384 sometimes matches 768 if you have a strong reranker. We'll validate empirically.
[06:45] Ruth: Any limits on embedding size in Hosted? We saw some providers cap dims or charge more.
[06:50] Maya: Hosted supports common dims up to 2048 but larger dims affect pricing. We'll include dimensionality in the pricing sheet.
[06:59] Nora: On the networking side, for Dedicated VPC peering, what are the setup steps and expected lead time?
[07:04] Diego: Usually 1-2 weeks for peering and securing firewall rules, plus another week for testing. For Private deployments it's longer. We'll provide a checklist.
[07:13] Ruth: Are there guardrails for data residency? We have EU users data that needs to stay in EU.
[07:18] Maya: Yes - you can pin region for Hosted and we have EU Dedicated clusters; Private gives full control.
[07:24] Ethan: What about realtime vs batch embedding generation? Some of our ETL runs nightly to index new docs.
[07:30] Diego: We support both. For realtime user queries you use the online endpoints; for batch you can hit batch ingestion APIs or run offline jobs using the same Dockerized sampler we provide.
[07:40] Ruth: Ok, I'm worried about cost during peak promos. Does Redwood offer burst capacity?
[07:45] Maya: Dedicated supports burst pools and autoscaling; we can also provision on demand for short windows but pricing will reflect that. For predictable budgets we can set hard caps.
[07:54] Nora: Any integrations with our existing OpenSearch to avoid duplicating documents?
[07:58] Diego: Yes you can keep canonical docs in OpenSearch and only store vectors in the vector DB; we provide middleware patterns and code examples to fetch BM25 results then augment with vector IDs.
[08:10] Ethan: On experimentation: can we A/B test embedding models and rerank thresholds?
[08:14] Maya: Yes - Redwood Console supports per-route model pins and canary rollouts. You can split traffic and view latency/cost/quality metrics.
[08:24] Ruth: Perfect. Let's talk risks: vendor lock, cost, and complexity. Any recommendations?
[08:29] Diego: To mitigate lock, we recommend keeping canonical vectors exportable and using standard vector formats; we'll provide export utilities. For cost, the pilot benchmarking will surface actual unit economics. For complexity, we offer integration support and runbooks.
[08:43] Speaker 1: (brief crosstalk, inaudible)
[08:48] Maya: Quick recap and next steps - we'll send pricing and security docs, Diego will draft benchmark plan, Nora will share sample data, and we'll schedule the benchmark the week of 4/27.
[08:59] Ruth: Sounds good. Anything else from us?
[09:03] Ethan: Can you include example cost per 100k queries with 768 vs 1536 dims in the pricing sheet?
[09:08] Maya: Yes we'll include that.
[09:11] Nora: I'll aim to upload the dataset today or tomorrow.
[09:14] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff. Thanks everyone.

End of call.
